defaults.teacher_persona: A service-desk lead who judges the reasoning, not the answer, and asks 'what did the user see?' before accepting any diagnosis.
classmates: A candidate on their capstone who wants to be told the mark scheme rather than work it out
A peer reviewer playing a difficult end user while the candidate works the ticket
defaults.interaction: Assessment-style: the teacher hands over a ticket or an artefact, the candidate works it aloud, and the peers push back the way a real queue, user, or reviewer would.
defaults.assessment: Each classroom ends with 3-5 checks aligned to the chapter's graded activity.

classrooms.title: Prove You Can Run Support
classrooms.prompt: Unpack the capstone brief: a portfolio that shows reasoning, not just answers. Have the classmates draft the structure of their own portfolio, then rehearse the professional-practice expectations — documentation, handover notes, and honesty about what they did not know.
objectives: Turn the capstone brief into a portfolio structure
Document a fix so another technician could repeat it
State the limits of your own knowledge without losing the room

activities.title: The brief, the portfolio, the standard

classrooms.title: Work the Queue
classrooms.prompt: Run a live service desk: a queue of tickets with different impact and urgency, a knowledge base to write into, and a user waiting. The candidate must prioritise, communicate, fix, and update the ticket — while a peer plays a user who gives incomplete information and then escalates.
objectives: Prioritise a queue by impact, urgency, and age
Ask the questions that turn a vague report into a reproducible fault
Keep the ticket and the user informed while you work

activities.title: Handover: what the next shift needs

classrooms.title: The Whole Ladder, One Page
classrooms.prompt: Consolidate ITSP101 through ITSP104 into the one-page map of the track, then run a certification review built from the candidate's own weak spots: the teacher pulls questions from earlier chapters, the peers mark the reasoning, and the group names what still needs work before the final exam.
objectives: Map each course in the track to its core skill
Answer a cross-track question using evidence from earlier chapters
Identify and close your own remaining gaps before the final exam

activities.title: My gap list, and what I do about it
